_note: Narrative for the ISA/IEC 62443-2-4:2023 service provider security programme assessment. Boilerplate inserted VERBATIM; the executive summary is composed by slot-substitution only (no free-writing). The instrument framing supplies the 'About this assessment' prose; this pack adds the composed executive summary, a caveat box and the consultant blocks. Aim: an achieved-maturity PROFILE across the functional areas in scope, never a single grade, with not-met and lowest-maturity requirements surfaced as floor findings. Audience: an asset owner assessing a provider, or a provider checking its own readiness, so the subject is always 'the service provider' and never assumed to be the client. Two caveats are carried: not a certification, and any demonstrated level conforms under the standard.

boilerplate.report_intro: This report presents a maturity assessment of a service provider's security programme against ISA/IEC 62443-2-4:2023. It covers the processes the provider can offer an asset owner when it integrates or maintains an automation solution. The report gives the maturity achieved for each base requirement and enhancement in the functional areas in scope, and a prioritised roadmap for the requirements that are not met or are at the lowest maturity. Other parts of the series cover the asset owner's own security programme and the security of the products used.
boilerplate.not_certification_caveat: This is a maturity assessment of a service provider's security programme against ISA/IEC 62443-2-4:2023. The consultant placed each base requirement and enhancement at one maturity level using the ML anchors, and the results form an achieved-maturity profile across the functional areas in scope, with no single grade. It does not certify the provider or state conformance. IEC does not certify against the standard, and any certificate comes from an independent scheme. Under the standard a requirement conforms at whichever maturity level the provider can demonstrate, ML1 included, so a requirement that is not met is the finding and the higher levels describe how mature the process is. The achieved maturity reflects what could be demonstrated at the time of the engagement.
boilerplate.series_context: ISA/IEC 62443 is a series of standards, divided according to who is responsible for what. This part, 62443-2-4, deals with the service provider who integrates or maintains an automation solution for an asset owner. The provider may be a system integrator, a maintenance contractor, a product supplier's service arm, an operator working on the owner's behalf or the owner's own in-house team. Its companions are 62443-2-1, which covers the asset owner's own security programme, and 62443-4-1, which covers the product supplier's development process.

executiveSummary._note: Composed by slot-substitution only; boilerplate VERBATIM; consultant blocks seeded with data-derived facts plus a marked placeholder. No free-writing. Order: verdict, scope + profile, gap-shape, profile-method + stakes, path forward + confidence. Works with or without the optional target-ML overlay, and with functional areas set out of scope.

templates.exec_verdict_nogaps: This assessment maps the maturity of the service provider security programme against ISA/IEC 62443-2-4:2023 and sets out the achieved-maturity profile across the functional areas in scope. Every requirement assessed is met at some maturity level.
templates.exec_scope: The assessment rated {answeredCount} of the {applicableCount} applicable requirements across {elementCount} functional areas.
templates.exec_profile: The achieved-maturity profile is {ml1} at ML1, {ml2} at ML2, {ml3} at ML3 and {ml4} at ML4, with {notMet} not met.
templates.exec_profile_targets: Against the target maturity set for the service, {meeting} of {compared} assessed requirements meet their target and {below} fall short.
templates.exec_path_forward: The roadmap in this report starts with the requirements that are not met, then raises maturity where it most affects the asset owner's system.
templates.exec_confidence: Coverage is {coveragePct} of the applicable requirements ({confidenceLabel}). Mean maturity is shown for context only. A not-met requirement is reported separately as a floor finding, so the mean cannot hide it.

gapConcentrationFragments.lowMaturity: The functional areas with the most requirements not met or at ML1 are {lowMaturityList}.

boilerplate.exec_profile_method: ISA/IEC 62443-2-4:2023 places each base requirement and each enhancement at its own maturity level (ML1 Initial, ML2 Managed, ML3 Defined / Practiced, ML4 Improving). The results form a profile with no single grade. A provider can be strong in one functional area and weak in another, and an average would hide the gaps that matter most to the asset owner.
boilerplate.stakes: Maturity describes how reliably the provider performs a process for the asset owner. A requirement that is not met is a process the provider cannot offer at any level. Gaps in a provider's programme travel with its people and tools onto the asset owner's system. Weak account handling, uncontrolled remote access or untested backups become the asset owner's exposure as soon as the provider starts work.
